findings.title: Changing RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE breaks documented/established exit code contract
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was changed from 4 to 3, and FEATURE_DISABLED was introduced as 4. This changes the exit code semantics for the `check` command. Any external scripts or CI/CD pipelines built against the previous exit code mapping (4 = recreate required) will now behave incorrectly, interpreting 'feature disabled' as 'recreate needed' or vice versa. Since this tool is explicitly documented for scripting purposes, exit code changes are a backward-incompatible break and should be called out prominently in release notes, not silently remapped during a preview-stage PR.

findings.title: Exit code table lists code 4 for feature disabled but doesn't mention 3 was reused for recreate
findings.body: The doc table now lists exit code 3 for 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible' (recreate) and 4 for feature disabled. This is consistent with the new CompatibilityResult constants, but the PR silently changed the recreate exit code from 4 to 3 without highlighting this as a breaking change to consumers relying on the previous mapping documented in earlier releases.

findings.title: Feature flag only enabled when updateStrategy is non-null
findings.body: In createInitialDeployment, the ROLLING_UPDATES feature is only enabled inside the `if (updateStrategy == null) return kc;` early-return branch skips feature enabling entirely for the null case. Since the operator now requires rolling-updates feature to be enabled for the new update behavior (per docs), the null-strategy test path never enables the feature, meaning testImageChange/testCacheMaxCount with null strategy test the default/disabled-feature behavior only, potentially masking regressions in the new feature-gated behavior for the default case.
